title: Streaming: typed disconnect errors w/ request_id + docs on safe reconnect/retry patterns
author: Mateusz Zielinski
release_notes: - Go SDK: streaming errors now include request_id + status_code when available, and expose a specific StreamDisconnectError for mid-stream disconnects. - Docs: added guidance on safe retry/reconnect patterns for streaming (idempotency + avoiding duplicate side effects).
body: Context: This PR is part of the cross-language SDK parity work for streaming semantics and error taxonomy. We’ve had multiple reports (SUP-29505) of streaming disconnects behind proxies/load balancers where the Go SDK returned opaque io.EOF / net errors without request_id, making Support/oncall triage slow (INT-1182). Also, customers asked for clearer guidance on whether they should retry streaming calls, and under what conditions (avoid duplicated completions / side effects). What this PR does: (1) Introduces typed streaming error surfaces so callers can distinguish server-side HTTP failures (pre-stream) vs transport disconnects (mid-stream) vs user cancellation/timeouts. (2) Propagates request_id and status_code onto those error types whenever we can infer them from headers/initial response. (3) Adds docs + examples for safe retry patterns and reconnect guidance, with explicit idempotency considerations. Details: - New error types (package redwood): StreamDisconnectError (raised when the HTTP connection drops after streaming has started), StreamResponseError (raised when we receive a non-2xx before streaming begins; wraps the existing APIError shape and includes request_id/status_code/error_code), and StreamCancelledError (wrapping context.Canceled / deadline exceeded so users can distinguish client-driven aborts from server disconnects). - request_id sourcing: for pre-stream errors, request_id comes from the JSON error payload when present, falling back to the X-Request-Id response header; for mid-stream disconnects, we attach request_id from the initial response headers captured at stream start (if we got that far), otherwise request_id is empty and callers should log their own correlation ID as well. - status_code behavior: StreamResponseError always has status_code; StreamDisconnectError sets status_code to 200 when we successfully established the stream and later disconnected (since the HTTP status was OK) and includes a reason string populated from the underlying error (EOF, read: connection reset, unexpected FIN, etc.). - Retry guidance (docs): We intentionally do NOT auto-retry mid-stream because replaying a generation can duplicate user-visible output and can duplicate side effects when tool/function calls are involved. The docs now recommend: (a) retries are safe only when the request failed before any tokens/events were delivered (StreamResponseError) and only for retryable status codes (429/5xx) using the shared retry policy; (b) for mid-stream disconnects (StreamDisconnectError) treat it as a partial result; if you must resume, restart a new request using application-level state (messages so far, partial text) and ensure your downstream side effects are idempotent; (c) for any retried request that could cause side effects, set an Idempotency-Key header and persist it per user action so retries dedupe on the server where supported. - Examples: Added a small snippet showing how to log request_id and differentiate disconnect vs retryable HTTP error. - Tests: Added unit tests that simulate: non-2xx error payload with X-Request-Id header; mid-stream disconnect after N events; and cancellation via context.WithCancel. Tests assert error types and fields (request_id/status_code) and verify we don’t leak API key in error strings. Why now: This was a top gap in the parity matrix (streaming edge cases + request_id propagation) and blocked docs updates and support macros. Follow-ups: - Conformance suite: we should add a fixture that forces a streaming disconnect and asserts the error surface matches other SDKs (tracked in ENG-5127). - Platform: ensure request_id is always present on initial streaming response headers even for proxy-buffered clients (see platform PR redwood/pr-28426). Checklist: - [x] Typed errors exposed for streaming paths - [x] request_id surfaced consistently and redaction-safe - [x] Docs updated w/ retry + idempotency guidance - [x] Unit tests for disconnect + cancellation - [x] CI green
commits: sdk(go): plumb request_id + status_code into streaming error path
docs(go): add streaming retry/reconnect guidance + idempotency notes
tests(go): simulate mid-stream disconnect and assert typed error fields
changed_files: streaming/client.go (capture initial response metadata; wrap disconnect/cancel errors)
examples/streaming/main.go (logging request_id, branching on error type)
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we make sure the disconnect error includes enough info to distinguish a 200-established stream vs a pre-stream failure? Also please avoid suggesting automatic retries for mid-stream disconnects—SRE is worried about duplicate billing concerns and replay storms. Mateusz (author): Yep—StreamDisconnectError will set status_code=200 if the stream was established and will include the underlying error cause; docs updated to explicitly say no auto-retry mid-stream and to treat it as partial output. Marcus Lin (review): Please confirm we never include the API key/token in error strings and the docs don’t encourage logging headers wholesale. Mateusz: Added redaction checks in tests and the example only logs request_id/status_code and the error type. Ibrahim Khan (review): Looks good for parity; can you also mention Idempotency-Key usage and that it must be stable per user action? Mateusz: Added a dedicated section in docs and a small code snippet. Sabrina James (review): Minor: can we align the field naming in docs with Python/TS (request_id, status_code) and call out that request_id can be missing if disconnect happens before headers? Mateusz: Updated wording and added the caveat. Approvals: Allison ✅, Marcus ✅, Ibrahim ✅, Sabrina ✅
